statement_record.book: For a pushout square with f : U → V, g : U → W, h : V → P, k : W → P, and every object X of C, the hom-set C(P,X) is the pullback in Set of C(h,X) and C(k,X) over C(f,X), C(g,X): a map out of P is precisely a pair of maps out of V and W agreeing after restriction along U.
statement_record.intree: ∃! u : pushout_apex P ~> Q, u ∘ pushout_in1 P ≈ q1 ∧ u ∘ pushout_in2 P ≈ q2  (given q1 ∘ f ≈ q2 ∘ g)
statement_record.strength_comparison: same (up to presentation): the ∃! quantified over every target Q and every compatible pair (q1,q2) is precisely the statement that u ↦ (u ∘ h, u ∘ k) is a bijection from C(P,X) onto {(a,b) ∈ C(V,X) × C(W,X) | a ∘ f = b ∘ g}, i.e. onto the Set-pullback; existence gives surjectivity and uniqueness gives injectivity (pushout_med_eq is the injectivity half in usable form). The only presentational difference is that the library never exhibits the Set-level pullback square itself, because it constructs no general pullbacks in Sets; nothing is weakened, since the elementwise form carries exactly the same content over hom-setoids with ≈.

statement_record.book: An X-shaped generalized element of A is a morphism a : X → A; C(−,A) sends X to the set of X-shaped elements, and Yoneda full-faithfulness means nothing about A is lost by replacing it with this functor. Two consequences: (a) a parallel pair f, g : A ⇒ B is equal as soon as it induces the same function on generalized elements of every shape; (b) a cone with summit A is a limit cone as soon as, for generalized elements of every shape, the induced functions form a limit cone in Set.

statement_record.book: Show that the isomorphism (3.5.1), lim_J C(X, F−) ≅ Cone(X, F), is natural in X.
statement_record.intree: wlim_natural (c c' : C) (h : c' ~{C}~> c) (α : W ⟹ HomDiagram c F) : to (wlim_iso c') (nat_compose (HomDiagram_precompose h F) α) ≈ to (wlim_iso c) α ∘ h — discharged for W = Δ[J](1) by conical_of_limit
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker (extra hypothesis, and the wrong two of the three legs). The library proves naturality in the apex for BOTH composites through the limit — lim_J C(X,F−) ≅ C(X, lim F) (conical_of_limit's wlim_natural, with [[[J,Sets]]](Δ(1), HomDiagram X F) as the standard Set-presentation of lim_J C(X,F−)) and Cone(X,F) ≅ C(X, lim F) (LimitIsUniversalProperty) — from which the exercise's naturality follows by cancellation. But both require the limit of F to EXIST IN C, whereas Riehl's (3.5.1) is unconditional: it needs only the limit of the Set-valued diagram C(X,F−). The direct bijection cone_of_nat / nat_of_cone (Structure/Limit/Weighted.v:145 and :157), which is (3.5.1) itself, is constructed but has no naturality lemma and is not even shown to be a bijection outside the WeightedLimit packaging.

gap: Missing: a naturality statement for the bijection (3.5.1) itself. In-tree, cone_of_nat / nat_of_cone convert between Δ(1) ⟹ HomDiagram X F and ACone X F but no lemma says this conversion commutes with reindexing along h : X' ~> X (i.e. with HomDiagram_precompose on one side and ConePresheaf's fmap on the other). Naturality is proved only for the two composites that factor through C(X, lim F), which presupposes that F has a limit in C — a hypothesis Riehl's (3.5.1) does not need.

evidence.intree_statement: Class Monic {x y} (f : x ~> y) := { monic : ∀ z (g1 g2 : z ~> x), f ∘ g1 ≈ f ∘ g2 → g1 ≈ g2 }.  (For every probe z this is exactly the injectivity of C(z,f) : C(z,x) → C(z,y), g ↦ f ∘ g.)
Class Epic {x y} (f : x ~> y) := { epic : ∀ z (g1 g2 : y ~> z), g1 ∘ f ≈ g2 ∘ f → g1 ≈ g2 }.  (For every probe z this is exactly the injectivity of C(f,z) : C(y,z) → C(x,z), g ↦ g ∘ f.)
Lemma injectivity_is_monic {X Y : SetoidObject} (f : X ~{Sets}~> Y) : (∀ x y : X, f x ≈ f y → x ≈ y) ↔ Monic f.

statement_record.book: Explain how monomorphisms and epimorphisms in an arbitrary category C are both defined representably in terms of monomorphisms (injections) in Set: f is monic iff C(X,f) is injective for every X, and epic iff C(f,X) is injective for every X.
statement_record.intree: Monic f := ∀ z (g1 g2 : z ~> x), f ∘ g1 ≈ f ∘ g2 → g1 ≈ g2;  Epic f := ∀ z (g1 g2 : y ~> z), g1 ∘ f ≈ g2 ∘ f → g1 ≈ g2;  injectivity_is_monic : (∀ x y, f x ≈ f y → x ≈ y) ↔ Monic f in Sets
statement_record.strength_comparison: same (up to presentation). Both in-tree classes ARE the representable conditions: the cancellation law for Monic, quantified over the probe z, is literally the injectivity of post-composition, i.e. of the action of the covariant hom-functor [Hom z,─] on f (Functor/Hom.v:60 defines that action as g ↦ f ∘ g); dually for Epic and the contravariant hom [Hom ─,z] (g ↦ g ∘ f). injectivity_is_monic supplies the remaining half of the exercise, that injectivity in Sets is exactly monicity there, so 'defined in terms of monomorphisms in Set' is literal. The only presentational difference is that no in-tree constant packages the round trip as a single biconditional 'Monic f ↔ ∀ z, Monic (fmap[[Hom z,─]] f)'; the two sides are definitionally the same proposition, so nothing is weakened. Note in passing that the converse Sets fact surjectivity_is_epic (Instance/Sets.v:429) is deliberately unfinished, but the exercise never needs it — its point is precisely that BOTH notions reduce to injections.

verifier.notes: Blind pass landed PARTIAL-leaning-PRESENT; I settle on PRESENT with the classifier. These ARE the representable conditions: Functor/Hom.v:60 `Curried_Hom` acts on morphisms by post-composition, so `monic` is verbatim the injectivity of C(z,f) for every probe z, and dually `epic` is the injectivity of C(f,z).
